# Shutdown and Trade Risk

**Summary.** Our season ends 2027-03-28, so late-season rest days and shutdowns hit our playoff weeks 19 to 21 directly. The trade deadline of 2027-03-04 falls before those weeks, so any deal that changes a role is settled before the playoffs. Discount veterans on teams with no reason to win in March, mostly the five teams without their own pick and any team that starts to tank. Plan FAB for the young players who could inherit minutes when a veteran is moved.

## Why our March 28 end raises the stakes

Our playoffs are weeks 19, 20 and 21, and the season ends on 2027-03-28. Late-season rest and shutdowns happen in March, so they land on the weeks that decide our title. Once a team decides to tank, an injured player can be shut down for the rest of the season even if he could have come back. ([08-17](https://youtu.be/LcZcvk8s1xQ?t=890))

A team with no reason to lose and no reason to win in March can cut veteran minutes to develop young players. For us, this means a veteran's full-season projection overstates what he gives in playoff weeks. Count a March minutes cut as a real cost, not a small detail. ([09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220))

Trades work the other way. The deadline is 2027-03-04, more than a week before week 19 starts. Any deal that changes a player's role is done before our playoffs, so a trade is a role risk for the veteran and a chance for the player behind him. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397))

## Which teams to watch

Teams that do not control their own pick have no reason to tank and no downside from losing. The notes name the Nets, Bucks, Clippers, Pelicans and Mavericks. Brooklyn and Milwaukee are called the main examples. These teams may rest players, be extra careful with injuries, or give young players developmental minutes late in the season. ([08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333))

Even without a pick to protect, these teams may still lean on young players and protect injured ones late in the season. So a veteran on one of these five teams carries March risk even if the team is not tanking. ([07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=127))

The second group is any team that starts to tank. Here the risk is an injury that turns into a season-ending shutdown. Check the standings in February. A bad team with an injured veteran is the clearest shutdown warning. ([08-17](https://youtu.be/LcZcvk8s1xQ?t=890))

## How to price risk at the auction

For stars on bad teams, a price range should include the risk, not just the per-game value. Bad teams may rest stars and cut their minutes. At our auction on 2026-10-18, bid below a player's per-game value when he plays for a weak team or a team without its own pick. Do not pay full price for March games that may never happen. ([09-30](https://youtu.be/MUbNYdjpUDM?t=372), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220))

Projections assume that trade candidates stay all season. So for a veteran with a trade tag, ask two questions before you bid. Would a trade to a contender make him a lesser option? Would a trade free up minutes for a young teammate you can buy for 1 USD or pick up on waivers? ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397))

Fill your 10 starter spots with players whose value does not depend on March. Use the 2 bench spots and late dollars for risky veterans at a discount, or for young players who could gain minutes after the deadline. ([09-30](https://youtu.be/MUbNYdjpUDM?t=372), [09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397))

## Young players who gain from a trade

Because projections keep trade candidates on their teams all season, they can understate the rookies and young players behind them. This is where cheap value hides. Before the 2027-03-04 deadline, list the young players who sit behind each veteran trade candidate you face or own. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397))

When a trade happens, act fast. Waivers process daily and you get at most 6 acquisitions per week, so keep FAB budget and a free move for deadline week. Teams without their own pick may also give young players developmental minutes in March, which makes their young players worth a look even without a trade. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397), [08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=127))

## In-season plan before the deadline

From January, check each veteran on your roster against three things: does his team control its pick, is the team losing, and is he carrying an injury. If two of the three are true, try to trade him before 2027-03-04 for a player on a team that is still pushing for wins. Trades are frequent in our league, so the deal is often there. ([08-17](https://youtu.be/LcZcvk8s1xQ?t=890), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333), [09-30](https://youtu.be/MUbNYdjpUDM?t=372))

Use the IL slots for injured players on teams that are still competing. An injured veteran on a tanking team may never return before March 28, so he should not hold an IL spot into the playoffs. ([08-17](https://youtu.be/LcZcvk8s1xQ?t=890))

## Where the notes differ

The notes agree on the direction but differ on what drives it. One view is that teams without their own pick have no reason to tank, so the risk is mainly rest and extra caution with injuries. The other view puts more weight on development: these teams may cut veteran minutes to lean on young players in March. In practice, both views lower a veteran's playoff value. The development view also raises the value of the young players on the same team. The player lines below also show expert splits on whether some trades will happen at all. ([08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=127), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220))
